(R268)(3) listed "an excluded zero as the dominant element of C's tie set" among what the configuration statement carries; zeroSide_neg_at_rate (SIDE-explicit-formula v0.27, RateIndex.lean :113-:126) takes no such argument and no line of its proof (:127-:188) reads one -- the limit form takes it (PowerLimit.lean :1082-:1083, consumed through coeffs_exist :1086 and the positive tie sum :1088), the rate form does not, and hrate's left side, never negative, already forces the tie set non-empty. Seen on reading the ζ proof line by line before any Lean; the author struck the clause as the navigator's (relay data/b658_author_answers.txt), and the statement carries no excluded-zero hypothesis.

(b) THE NAVIGATOR'S: A BRANCH NAMED FOR DELETION THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The ferry's step zero names SIDE-lv-conservation push-b657-runner; it stands neither locally nor at the remote (git branch --list and git branch -r at step zero), and b657's closing names push-b657-merge alone in that kernel (relay data/b657_closing.txt :100, :142-:144). Nothing deleted under that name; the branches that stood were deleted by name after --merged listed them.

(c) THE NAVIGATOR'S: A RUNNER WHOSE PRINT STEP COULD NOT REACH THE NEW THEOREMS. (R268)(4) dispatches to the workflow on main from b654; its print step names E1's three terminals in its own text (SIDE-explicit-formula main, .github/workflows/build-module.yml :77-:83), so the configuration theorems could not be printed without a write to the kernel's main before the merge, which N5 bars. Seen on reading the workflow before the statement prompt; the author's word: the print step reads print_targets.txt at the kernel's root, the branch carries the edit and the file, the dispatch is at the branch, and the merge carries both -- standing under (R263)(4) for every kernel's runner at its next use.

(d) THE SEAT'S: A READ-FIRST BANKED LATE. The ferry's read-first list was read and cited in the banks that rest on it (the statement bank's sections 1-3, relay data/b658_e1cfg_statement.txt) before any Lean, but its own bank, cited by path and line with each bank's row unit named (b657's form, data/b657_readfirst.txt), was written after Component 4 (relay data/b658_readfirst.txt), not before Component 1. Caught on carrying b657's suite, before the seal; the bank written then, every citation in it re-read at its blob.

(e) THE SEAT'S: A DELETE ON A VARIABLE PATH. The local check of the print step (relay data/b658_commands.txt #82, before the commit on the branch) made a temporary directory by `mktemp -d`, copied print_targets.txt into it, ran the extracted step there, and removed it by `rm -rf "$d"` -- a delete naming a shell variable, not a verified absolute path in the same command, against the standing delete rule (scratch files included). The directory was the mktemp one and nothing else was removed; G-EDIT-ROUTE reads the command as an offence and fails on real state at HEAD, declared on the face by name before the lock. Not repairable after the fact; the next scratch check names its directory by absolute path in the delete's own command.

(f) THE SEAT'S: A STRAY sed -i. A compile check of the record tool (relay data/b658_commands.txt #107, before the seal) opened with `sed -i 's/x/x/' /dev/null` -- a no-op on no file of any tree, which failed (/dev/null not a regular file) and wrote nothing -- but a sed -i all the same, against the edit route (every file the seat writes through the Edit tool, never sed). G-EDIT-ROUTE reads it as a second offence; declared on the face with (e) before the lock.
